theater: 長安大明宮禁中與御苑

battle.name: 甘露之變
battle.theater: 長安大明宮禁中與御苑
battle.brief: 太和九年（835）十一月，宰相李訓與鄭注以「甘露降於御苑石榴樹」為由，把唐文宗與百官召入大明宮禁中，企圖趁典禮埋伏神策軍行刺，事敗，黨羽盡誅。卡面羅馬標槍屬帝國軍團的投槍，形制早於大唐數百年，不可能出現在長安宮廷；當夜真正用得上的，是禁軍手邊的刀、槊、弩與火炬。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 這場衝突發生在唐王朝的宮禁之內，沒有跨國交戰，交戰的兩方都是大唐朝廷內部的政治集團。宮廷一方以皇帝唐文宗李昂為名義核心，實際的武力與指揮權握在內侍監王守澄與內侍監仇士良手中，左右神策軍、內衙禁軍以及金吾衛、宮門宿衛都聽命於宦官系統；文宗久病，起居行動都依賴內侍省安排。陰謀一方以宰相李訓與方士出身的鄭注為核心，兩人藉講經、符籙與藥術取得文宗信任，合稱「李鄭」，在朝中拉攏御史、臺官與翰林學士，並私下勾結神策軍中可以被買通的將士與死士。事成之後李訓打算把神策軍握成自己的資本、趕走宦官，鄭注則志在直接掌兵，兩人對此並不一致。旁觀者中還有宰相李逢吉與牛僧孺所代表的牛黨：鄭注最初正是由李逢吉引薦給文宗的，但事變之後李逢吉改與宦官合作，成為清算李訓一系最積極的人。外鎮並未卷入，河北、劍南、河東的節度使各守本鎮，沒有動兵勤王，也沒有借機問鼎；整場政變始終局限在長安城內的宮院與街坊之間，未曾演成任何形式的地方戰爭。
countriesEn: This clash took place inside the palace precincts of the Tang dynasty, with no fighting between states: the two sides were political groups within the Tang court itself. The palace side had Emperor Wenzong of Tang, Li Ang, as its nominal centre, but the real military power and command lay with the eunuch directors Wang Shoucheng and Qiu Shiliang, who commanded the Left and Right Shence Armies, the imperial guards of the inner commands, the Gate Guards and the night watch of the palace precinct; the emperor was chronically ill and relied on the Directorate of Palace Affairs for the conduct of his daily life. The conspiratorial side was led by the chancellor Li Xun and by Zheng Zhu, a Daoist adept of medicine and talismans. The two men gained the emperor's trust through lecturing on the classics, through talismanic arts and through medicine, and were known collectively as Li and Zheng; they drew in censorial officials, the men of the Censorate and Hanlin Academy, and privately bought over soldiers and desperate men inside the Shence Army. Should the plan succeed, Li Xun intended to turn the Shence Army into his own instrument and drive the eunuchs out, while Zheng Zhu aimed at holding the troops directly; the two were not of one mind on this. Among the bystanders were the chancellor Li Fengji and Niu Sengru, who headed the Niu faction: Zheng Zhu had originally been introduced to Wenzong by Li Fengji, yet after the affair Li Fengji joined hands with the eunuchs and became the most zealous in the purge of Li Xun's group. The provincial military governors were not drawn in: the jiedushi of Hebei, Jiannan and Hedong each stayed within their own circuits, none rose to march on the capital and none used the confusion to bid for the throne. The whole conspiracy remained confined to the palace precincts and the wards of Chang'an, and never developed into a provincial war in any form.
people: 主角是幾個身處權力核心的人。第一個是唐文宗李昂，827 年至 840 年在位，性好儒術，屢次想削弱宦官，又自認無法控制神策軍；他長期被風疾與心病折磨，說話都難以成句，最後幾乎全靠內侍省替他傳話與發號施令，甘露之變正是他在諸次削藩與除宦都告失敗之後，一次孤注一擲的自救。第二個是宰相李訓，出身北方武職家庭，歷任御史、侍講，因直言敢諫與通曉權謀受到文宗倚重，太和九年升任同平章事，企圖用一次成功的宮廷突擊換取皇帝對自己的全面信任。第三個是鄭注，一個精通符籙與醫方的方士，靠神術與藥物博得文宗歡心，被授官並經手部分禁軍調度，是刺殺計畫的實際執行者；事敗當夜他改名換姓躲入市井，最終仍被搜捕。第四個是內侍監仇士良，他長期掌控神策軍並深受文宗倚信，事前已察覺異常而暗中戒備，關鍵時刻搶在陰謀者之前控制宮門與禁軍，反而成了保住皇帝的人。第五個是內侍監王守澄，掌內侍省並兼管部分禁軍，是事後清算與扶立新帝的重要推手。此外還有牛黨領袖牛僧孺與李逢吉，以及在會昌朝主持清算牛黨的宰相李德裕；唐武宗李炎在兄長死後即位，把文宗未竟的削藩事業推到最高點。事後記錄這場事變的主要是《舊唐書》與《新唐書》，司馬光《資治通鑑》卷二百四十六把經過寫得最細，後人稱引的「甘露之變」一詞即出自這類記載。
peopleEn: The protagonists were a handful of people at the very centre of power. The first was Emperor Wenzong of Tang, Li Ang, who reigned from 827 to 840. Fond of Confucian learning, he repeatedly tried to weaken the eunuchs yet never felt able to control the Shence Army; he suffered for years from a paralytic illness and a heart complaint, could barely get his words out, and in the end relied almost entirely on the Directorate of Palace Affairs to speak and to act for him. The Sweet Dew affair was his single desperate attempt at self-rescue after every effort at reducing the regional governors and removing the eunuchs had failed. The second was the chancellor Li Xun, of a northern military family, who had served as a censor and as a lecturer at court and won Wenzong's trust by his blunt remonstrance and his mastery of court politics; in 835 he was raised to the post of chancellor in the same rank of affairs, hoping that one successful blow inside the palace would buy him the emperor's complete confidence. The third was Zheng Zhu, a Daoist adept skilled in talismans and medicine who pleased Wenzong with his arts and his drugs, was given office and a say in the movement of some of the imperial guards, and was the man who would actually carry out the killing; on the night of the failure he changed his name and hid among the shops of the city, and was finally hunted down. The fourth was the eunuch director Qiu Shiliang, who had long controlled the Shence Army and was trusted by Wenzong; he had already sensed that something was wrong and kept his own guard, and at the decisive moment he seized the palace gates and the guards ahead of the conspirators and so became the man who saved the emperor. The fifth was the eunuch director Wang Shoucheng, who headed the Directorate of Palace Affairs and controlled part of the guards, and who was the driving force behind the purge afterwards and the elevation of the new emperor. Others include the Niu faction leaders Niu Sengru and Li Fengji, and Li Deyu, the chancellor who presided over the destruction of the Niu faction during the Huichang reign; Li Yan, Emperor Wuzong, succeeded his brother and carried Wenzong's unfinished work of reducing the governors as far as it could be pushed. The event itself is recorded chiefly in the Jiu Tangshu and the Xin Tangshu, while Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian, in volume 246, gives the fullest account; the phrase Sweet Dew Incident used by later writers comes from just such records.
kits: 卡面上這支羅馬標槍（pilum）是共和國晚期到帝國早期軍團的標準投槍：木製長桿前端套一段約六十公分的軟鐵槍莖，槍莖與木桿以鉚釘固定，軟鐵受力後會彎折，插在盾牌上的部分便折斷留在盾面，盾兵要拔掉它、重整盾緣才能繼續作戰；全槍連桿接近兩公尺，重量約一公斤，拋擲距離可達二三十公尺，戰術用途不是單純殺傷，而是先打亂對方盾線、遮蔽盾後視線，讓己方弓兵在對手抬頭之前完成射擊。這套東西在 835 年的大唐宮廷裡從未出現：它不屬於唐代兵器譜系，長安宮中也沒有任何一支羅馬式投槍的實物或仿製品。當晚真正用得上的，是禁軍與神策軍手邊的近身兵器：唐刀與儀刀、柄裝的陌刀、長柄的槊與戟，還有手弓、角弓與臂弩；唐代步軍裝備條目裡同類的標槍長約一丈，兼具刺與擲兩用，是唯一在形制上可以與羅馬標槍對照的兵器，但它同樣沒有出現在甘露之變的記載中。防具方面，神策軍穿明光甲與魚鱗、鎖子之屬，戴兜鍪，配圓盾與拒馬；照明靠火炬與燭，因典禮在深秋夜裡舉行，宮門與廊下火把連成一片。甘露典禮本身還需要一批儀仗道具：擬詔的紙筆、承露的玉盤與寶瓶，以及控制人流用的戟、鞭與門鎖。整場衝突沒有攻城器，沒有投石，也沒有運輸問題，最吃緊的物資其實是火把、燈油與馬料，以及能否把數百人同時塞進狹窄的宮門。
kitsEn: The Roman pilum on the card is the standard javelin of the late Republican and early Imperial legion: a long wooden shaft with a soft-iron tang of about sixty centimetres fitted to its front, the two joined by rivets, and the soft iron bending on impact so that the part stuck in a shield snaps off and stays there, forcing the shield-bearer to pull it out and re-form his shield wall before he can carry on. With the shaft the whole weapon runs close to two metres and weighs roughly a kilogram, and it can be thrown twenty to thirty metres. Its tactical purpose is not sheer killing but disruption: it breaks up the enemy's shield line and blinds the men behind it, so that the friendly archers can loose before the enemy can raise his head. None of this was present in the Tang court of 835. The pilum did not belong to the Tang armatarium, and there was in the palace at Chang'an neither a Roman javelin nor a copy of one. What was actually to hand on that night were the close-combat weapons of the guards and the Shence Army: Tang sabres and ceremonial blades, long-handled pole-blades, spears and halberds, together with hand bows, horn bows and crossbows. The one item in the Tang infantry list comparable in form was the biaochiang, a light javelin about three metres long that could be used either to thrust or to throw; it too does not appear in any record of the Sweet Dew affair. On the defensive side, the Shence Army wore minghuang plate and mail of the scale and ring kinds, carried helmets, and used round shields and caltrops. Illumination came from torches and candles, for the rite was held on a late autumn night and the torches along the gates and corridors made a continuous line of fire. The rite itself required a set of ceremonial props: paper and brush for drafting the edict, jade plates and precious vessels to receive the dew, and halberds, whips and door bolts for controlling the flow of people. There were no siege engines, no stone-throwers and no transport problems in the whole affair; the tightest supplies were in fact torches, lamp oil and fodder, and the question of whether several hundred people could be squeezed through the narrow palace gates at the same moment.
tactics: 這是一場在封閉宮院裡策劃的夜襲式政變，戰術核心不是野戰的進退，而是空間、節點與同步。策劃者利用「甘露降於御苑石榴樹」的天賜祥瑞作餌，由翰林擬詔、宣示百官，把皇帝、諸王與公卿從各處官署召到大明宮禁中的殿院與御苑一帶；典禮要人同時站立、同時上前迎取承露的寶瓶，這正是製造密集人群、把行刺對象與所有可能的目擊者壓進同一條通道的辦法。埋伏的兵力藏在殿門、廊廡與帷幕之後，兵器以刀、戟、槊為主，另有拉弓持弩者封住出入方向；關鍵是控制宮門與神策軍的指揮權，一旦內侍監仇士良察覺宮門守備被抽調、刀兵未按約定的時刻出現在帷幕之後，陰謀者便再無突然性。據《資治通鑑》所記，典禮當日忽起大風，帷幕被吹得歪斜，埋伏的人馬失去同時發動的默契，埋伏遂告洩漏；宦官一方搶先控制神策軍與幾道宮門，護著皇帝退入殿內，並調兵反擊，李訓所部在宮中廊下被殲。事後的處置同樣是宮廷式的：封閉宮門、封鎖坊門、清查同黨，捕獲者就地格殺或押赴刑場，凡與「李鄭」往來而罪證不實者則貶謫外放，藉此把一次未遂的宮廷陰謀變成一場整頓朝班的行動。
tacticsEn: This was a night assault plotted inside a sealed palace precinct, and its tactical core was not the manoeuvre of open battle but space, nodes and synchronisation. The plotters used the heavenly gift of sweet dew descending on the pomegranate trees of the imperial garden as bait: a Hanlin official drafted the edict, the announcement went out to the officials, and the emperor, the princes and the court were drawn from their offices to the courtyards and the garden of the palace precinct at Daming Palace. The rite required everyone to stand together and to step forward together to receive the precious vessel of dew, and that was precisely the way to pack a dense crowd and squeeze both the target and every possible witness into a single passage. The ambush troops were hidden behind the hall doors, along the covered walks and behind the curtains, armed mainly with sabres, halberds and pole-blades, while bowmen and crossbowmen covered the lines of exit. The decisive point was control of the palace gates and of the Shence command: the moment the eunuch director Qiu Shiliang noticed that the gate watch had been drawn off and that the blades had not come behind the curtains at the agreed hour, the conspirators had no surprise left. According to the Zizhi Tongjian, a great wind rose on the day of the rite, the curtains were blown askew, and the men waiting in ambush lost the timing that would have let them strike together, so the ambush was exposed; the eunuch side took the Shence Army and several palace gates first, escorted the emperor back into the hall and then counter-attacked, and Li Xun's men were cut down in the covered walks of the palace. The aftermath was equally of a piece with palace warfare: the gates were sealed, the ward gates locked, the associates searched out; those caught were killed on the spot or dragged to the execution ground, and those whose contact with Li and Zheng could not be proved were merely demoted and exiled, so that an unsuccessful palace conspiracy was turned into a purge of the court.
data: 能夠核對的數字不多，但有幾個硬指標。時間點是太和九年（835）十一月，按曆法換算落在西元 835 年 11 月末至 12 月之間。制度數字方面：神策軍始置於天寶十三載（754），由哥舒翰奏請成立，最初只千餘人，到中晚唐時護軍將軍所領兵眾合計被估在萬人上下，另有左右神武軍、左右威武軍等內衙禁軍，禁軍總額常被估為數萬人；宮中宦官在中晚唐為數百人至數千人規模不等，掌軍的內侍監不過數人，權力卻集中在他們手上。唐文宗自 827 年即位至 840 年崩，在位十三年，先後面對河北藩鎮的驕縱與朝臣之間的反覆傾軋，他親自圖謀的削藩與除宦都沒有成功。事變的直接參與人數，現存史籍沒有留下可靠記載，只能說百官隨帝集於宮中，埋伏人數以數十計，兵刃相接的規模是宮院內的數十對數十，而不是兩軍對陣；事後被誅者、伏法者與被貶謫者的確切人數，舊史與通鑑都只作概括敘述。分水嶺則在 840 年 12 月文宗崩後：相傳他被宦官毒死，仇士良以內侍監身份掌神策軍直到 846 年；同一套「甘露降」的引誘手法在會昌六年（846）前後又被人用了一次，這一次發動者是宦官集團、對象是唐宣宗，宣宗避開了典禮，陰謀敗露後有數十名相關的內侍與將領被誅。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked, but several are hard. The date is the eleventh month of Taihe year nine, 835, which converts to late November or December of 835 AD. On institutions and numbers: the Shence Army was first raised in the thirteenth year of Tianbao, 754, on the petition of Geshu Han, with only a thousand men or so at the start; by the middle and late Tang the troops under the guards commanders are commonly put at around ten thousand, with the Left and Right Divine Martial and Left and Right Valiant Martial Commands alongside them, and the total strength of the inner guards is often estimated in the tens of thousands. The eunuchs of the palace in the middle and late Tang numbered anywhere from several hundred to several thousand, but the directors who commanded troops were only a handful of men, and the power was concentrated in them. Wenzong reigned from 827 until his death in 840, thirteen years, facing the insubordination of the Hebei governors and the endless manoeuvring of his ministers; his own attempts to reduce the governors and to remove the eunuchs all failed. The number of men directly involved in the affair is not reliably recorded. All that can be said is that the officials assembled with the emperor in the palace, that the number waiting in ambush was on the order of a few tens, and that the clash of arms was on a scale of a few tens against a few tens inside palace courtyards, not two armies in the field; the exact number executed, killed in custody or demoted is given only in general terms by the old histories and the Tongjian. The watershed came after Wenzong's death in December 840: he is said to have been poisoned by the eunuchs, and Qiu Shiliang held the Shence Army as director until 846. The same lure of the descending sweet dew was used once more around the sixth year of Huichang, 846, but this time the eunuch party was the initiator and Tang Xuanzong the target; the emperor avoided the rite, the plot came to nothing, and several tens of the eunuchs and officers involved were put to death.
cause: 直接起因是一次錯估了敵意的宮廷冒險，根子則在唐朝中期以來的三重積弊。第一是宦官與禁軍的問題：安史之亂後宦官領兵、左右神策軍護駕有功，漸成皇帝倚重的主力，文宗削藩屢試不果後轉而想在宮內解決宦官，卻連自己的神策軍指揮權都握不穩。第二是黨爭：文宗在牛僧孺、李逢吉與李德裕之間維持平衡，李訓、鄭注正是靠倒向李德裕一派、並以才能與迎合取寵，才得到升至宰相的機會；一旦倒戈成功，黨爭就會再翻一頁，因此雙方都認為對方不會先讓步。第三是「祥瑞」作為政治語言的傳統：唐代以甘露、雲鶴、芝草為天意之驗，策劃者正是借這種語言把一次刺殺包裝成宮廷典禮，使皇帝在眾目睽睽之下走到指定的位置。至於李訓與鄭注之間的裂痕，則直接影響了計畫的細節與執行時的人心：鄭注自恃握兵，李訓卻仍要藉文宗之力完成對宦官的清洗，兩人各懷算計，命令到最後一刻仍不統一，為事後的全面崩潰埋下伏筆。文宗在甘露之變後得到的教訓，後人概括得很直白：以帝王之尊去對付掌握禁軍的人，輸的只能是皇帝自己。
causeEn: The immediate cause was a palace gamble that misjudged the resolve of the other side, and its roots lay in three accumulated evils of the middle Tang. First, the eunuchs and the guards: after the An Lushan rebellion the eunuchs took command of troops and the Left and Right Shence Armies earned their place as the emperor's protectors, so that by Wenzong's reign they had become the force the court relied on. After his attempts to reduce the provincial governors failed repeatedly, Wenzong turned to solving the eunuch problem inside the palace, yet he could not even be sure of his own command over the Shence Army. Second, factional strife: Wenzong held the balance between Niu Sengru, Li Fengji and Li Deyu, and Li Xun and Zheng Zhu rose to power precisely by turning to Li Deyu's side and by their ability and their flatteries, which brought them the chance to be made chancellors. If their side prevailed the factional contest would turn over another page, so each camp believed the other would not give way first. Third, the political language of auspicious omens: the Tang treated sweet dew, white cranes and fungus as proofs of heavenly favour, and it was by borrowing that language that the plotters dressed a murder up as a court rite, so that the emperor would walk to the appointed place before the eyes of the whole court. The fissure between Li Xun and Zheng Zhu also shaped the details of the plan and the mood of the men who had to execute it: Zheng Zhu counted on holding the troops, while Li Xun still needed the emperor's authority to finish off the eunuchs; each had his own calculation, and the orders were never unified even to the last moment, which laid up the collapse that followed. The lesson the affair taught Wenzong was later summed up bluntly: when an emperor tries to move against the men who hold the guards, the only one who loses is the emperor himself.
impact: 甘露之變的直接影響，是唐文宗失去了最後一次主動出擊的機會。事後，宦官集團以護駕有功為名接管了宮禁與神策軍，文宗本人的言行從此幾乎全在內侍省的安排之下；他在位最後幾年形同傀儡，兩度想借宰相與外藩的力制衡宦官，都被擋回。840 年 12 月文宗崩，傳言稱他被毒死，帝位由其弟李炎繼承，是為唐武宗。武宗朝在李德裕主持下先做了一場政治清算：牛黨領袖牛僧孺被貶往崖州，死在流放途中，鄭注、李訓一系的舊人相繼被貶外；隨後 843 年武宗用兵澤潞，攻下昭義軍，結束了中晚唐最後一個割據的藩鎮，第二年平定淮西，實現了文宗沒有完成的削藩。這條「內削宦官、外平藩鎮」的邏輯，最終在 846 年收到效果：唐宣宗李忱登基後反過來清洗宦官，數十名內侍與相關將領被殺；在此之前，「甘露」二字在宮廷中已經是陷阱與陰謀的代名詞。甘露之變因此成為中國史籍中「以祥瑞為名的宮門刺殺」的原型案例，後人談宮廷政變，往往先舉 835 年這一次。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the Sweet Dew affair was that Wenzong lost his last chance to strike on his own initiative. Afterwards the eunuch group, on the strength of having guarded the emperor, took over the palace precincts and the Shence Army, and the emperor's words and actions fell almost entirely under the arrangement of the Directorate of Palace Affairs; in the last years of his reign he was a puppet in all but name, and twice he tried to use the chancellors and the outlying governors to balance the eunuchs, and was blocked both times. When Wenzong died in December 840, reportedly poisoned, the throne passed to his brother Li Yan, who became Emperor Wuzong. The Huichang reign first carried out a political purge under Li Deyu: the Niu faction leader Niu Sengru was demoted to Yazhou and died in exile, and the surviving associates of Zheng Zhu and Li Xun were demoted and sent away in turn; then in 843 Wuzong campaigned against Zhaoyi, took the circuit of Leling, and ended the last separatist command of the middle and late Tang, and the following year he pacified Huai West, achieving the reduction of the governors that Wenzong had failed to complete. That logic of trimming the eunuchs inside and the governors outside finally produced results in 846: when Tang Xuanzong, Li Chen, came to the throne he turned the tables and purged the eunuchs, killing several tens of palace servants and the officers involved with them; by that point the two characters for sweet dew had already become, inside the palace, a synonym for trap and conspiracy. The Sweet Dew affair therefore stands as the archetype in Chinese historical writing of the murder at the palace gate disguised as an auspicious omen, and later discussions of palace coups generally begin by citing the year 835.
result: 結果是陰謀方全軍覆沒，宮廷方雖保住皇帝，卻沒有贏得任何東西。事變當夜，李訓、鄭注以及被拉進來的將士、臺官與死士被分別處置：現存史籍記載被誅者首要是李訓、鄭注二人，其餘黨羽或死於宮中廊下，或在追捕中被殺，或被貶謫到嶺南、塞外；沒有一支人馬逃出皇城，也沒有任何一位節度使起兵響應。皇帝唐文宗從此在宮中活著，卻再也沒有自己的兵。從戰術層面看，這是一次以吉兆為餌的夜襲，輸在三件事上：出兵的訊號由別人掌握，發動的時機被一場大風打亂，宮門的鑰匙握在宦官手裡。甘露從此在唐廷是一個危險的字眼，宮中再要行刺，誰都知道必須換一個說法；而對武器史而言，這一夜的短兵相接裡沒有出現任何一件重裝投擲兵器，連長兵器都很少出現，主流是刀、戟、槊、弩與火炬，與卡面那支羅馬標槍所代表的軍團投射兵器毫無關係。甘露之變真正留下的，是一堂關於宮禁夜戰、禁軍調度與京師護衛的實戰課。
resultEn: The conspirators were wiped out entirely, and the palace side, though it saved the emperor, won nothing for itself. On the night itself Li Xun, Zheng Zhu, and the soldiers, officials and desperate men who had been drawn in were dealt with separately: the old histories record that the principal names executed were Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, while the rest of the associates were killed in the covered walks of the palace, killed while being hunted, or demoted to Lingnan or the frontier. Not a single man escaped the imperial city, and not one provincial governor rose to answer the call. Emperor Wenzong went on living in the palace, but he never again had troops of his own. Tactically this was a night raid baited with an omen, and it lost on three counts: the signal for the attack was in other hands, the moment for the stroke was spoiled by a great wind, and the keys to the palace gates were held by the eunuchs. From then on the word sweet dew was a dangerous word at the Tang court, and anyone planning another assassination in the palace knew he would have to find another pretext. As for the history of arms, nothing heavy in the way of a missile weapon appeared in that night's close fighting; long weapons were rare too, and the staple was the sabre, halberd, pole-blade, crossbow and torch, with no relation at all to the Roman pilum on the card and the legionary missile weapon it stands for. What the Sweet Dew affair truly left behind was a field lesson in night fighting inside the palace precincts, in the movement of the guards, and in the defence of the capital.
